summary: When the Kohen Gadol went into the Heichal to bow down, three Kohanim held on to him. When he came out, his brothers the Kohanim went in to bow down too.
stIntro: After the priests concluded sacrificing the daily morning offering, they would enter the Sanctuary to prostrate themselves.

chunks.en: When the Kohen Gadol goes in to bow down,
chunks.st: On occasions when the High Priest would enter the Sanctuary to prostrate
chunks.stMore: himself, he would enter before the other priests.

chunks.en: three (Kohanim) hold on to him:
chunks.st: When the High Priest enters the Sanctuary, three priests hold him
chunks.stMore: to assist him and support him, in order to distinguish the service of the High Priest from that of the other priests entering the Sanctuary.

chunks.en: one by his right hand,
chunks.st: One priest held his right hand

chunks.en: one by his left hand,
chunks.st: and one priest held his left hand,

chunks.en: and one by the precious stones (on his shoulders).
chunks.st: and one priest stood behind the High Priest, holding onto the two precious onyx stones
chunks.stMore: located on the shoulders of the High Priest, on the ephod.

words.note: Two onyx stones on the shoulders of the Kohen Gadol's apron.

chunks.en: When the memuneh heard the sound of the feet
chunks.st: And once the appointed priest heard the sound from the feet

chunks.en: of the Kohen Gadol, that he is coming out,
chunks.explain: The Kohen Gadol's robe had bells on the bottom.
chunks.st: of the High Priest, produced by the bells attached to the bottom of his robe, he knew that the High Priest was emerging from the Sanctuary,

chunks.en: he lifted up the curtain for him.
chunks.st: and he lifted the curtain suspended at the opening of the Entrance Hall for him, to facilitate his exit.

chunks.en: He went in, bowed down, and went out,
chunks.st: After the High Priest entered and prostrated himself and emerged from the Sanctuary,

chunks.en: and his brothers the Kohanim went in, bowed down, and went out.
chunks.st: his brethren the priests entered, prostrated themselves, and emerged from the Sanctuary.

summary: The Kohanim stood on the steps of the Ulam and gave Birkas Kohanim. The mishnah explains how Birkas Kohanim in the Beis HaMikdash was different from everywhere else.
stIntro: After the priests emerged from the Sanctuary,

chunks.en: They came and stood on the steps of the Ulam.
chunks.st: they came and stood on the twelve stairs before the Entrance Hall.

chunks.en: The first ones stood to the south of their brothers the Kohanim,
chunks.st: The first five priests stood to the south of their brethren, the priests,
chunks.stMore: who had taken the limbs of the daily offering up to the altar.

chunks.en: with five vessels in their hands:
chunks.st: And those five priests had five vessels in their hands:

chunks.en: the teni in the hand of one,
chunks.st: The basket with the ashes from the inner altar was in the hands of one priest;

chunks.en: the kuz in the hand of one,
chunks.st: and the jug with the ashes from the Candelabrum was in the hands of one priest;

chunks.en: the fire pan in the hand of one,
chunks.st: and the coal pan was in the hands of one priest;

chunks.en: the bowl in the hand of one,
chunks.st: and the smaller vessel, the bowl that held the incense, was in the hands of one priest, who had burned the incense;

chunks.en: and the spoon and its cover in the hand of one.
chunks.st: and the spoon and its cover were in the hands of one
chunks.stMore: priest, the friend or relative of the one who burned the incense.

chunks.en: And they blessed the people with one bracha.
chunks.st: The priests placed their vessels on the ground and then blessed the people, reciting one blessing.
chunks.stMore: The Priestly Benediction was recited outside the Temple as well,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁבַּמְּדִינָה אוֹמְרִים אוֹתָהּ שָׁלשׁ בְּרָכוֹת,
chunks.en: But in the rest of the country they say it as three brachos,
chunks.st: but in the Temple, it was recited differently, as in the rest of the country the priests would recite it as three blessings,
chunks.stMore: and the listeners would answer amen after each blessing.

chunks.en: and in the Beis HaMikdash as one bracha.
chunks.st: But in the Temple they would recite it as one blessing,
chunks.stMore: and the listeners would not respond to each blessing. Rather, at the conclusion of the entire Priestly Benediction they would answer: Blessed are You Lord, God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.

chunks.he: בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים אֶת הַשֵּׁם כִּכְתָבוֹ,
chunks.en: In the Beis HaMikdash they said Hashem's Name as it is written,
chunks.st: In the Temple, the priests would recite the name of God as it is written, with the letters yod, heh, vav, heh,

words.note: Hashem's special Name, said only in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and in the rest of the country with its other name.
chunks.st: whereas in the rest of the country the priests would recite the name of God by His appellation, alef, dalet, nun, yod.

words.note: Another name for Hashem, the one we say in davening.

chunks.en: In the rest of the country the Kohanim lift up their hands,
chunks.st: Furthermore, in the rest of the country, while reciting the Priestly Benediction the priests lift their hands

chunks.en: their hands across from their shoulders,
chunks.st: opposite their shoulders,

chunks.en: and in the Beis HaMikdash above their heads,
chunks.st: and in the Temple they raise them above their heads.
chunks.stMore: That is the halakha with regard to all priests in the Temple,

chunks.en: except for the Kohen Gadol, who does not lift
chunks.st: except for the High Priest, who does not raise

chunks.en: his hands higher than the tzitz.
chunks.st: his hands above the frontplate
chunks.stMore: on his forehead, as the name of God is written on the frontplate.

words.note: The gold plate on the Kohen Gadol's forehead, with Hashem's Name on it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even the Kohen Gadol lifts
chunks.st: Even the High Priest would raise

chunks.en: his hands higher than the tzitz,
chunks.st: his hands above the frontplate
chunks.stMore: while reciting the Priestly Benediction in the Temple,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated with regard to the Priestly Benediction recited by Aaron the High Priest: “

chunks.en: "And Aharon lifted his hands
chunks.st: And Aaron lifted his hands

chunks.en: toward the people and blessed them."
chunks.st: toward the people and blessed them” (Leviticus 9:22).

summary: When the Kohen Gadol wanted to bring the korban himself, the Segan helped him up the ramp and the Kohanim handed him the parts. Then came the wine, the trumpets, the cymbal and the song of the Levi'im. The mishnah ends with a tefillah that the Beis HaMikdash be rebuilt soon.
stIntro: The High Priest is entitled to sacrifice any offering brought to the Temple, at his discretion.

chunks.en: When the Kohen Gadol wants to burn (the korban),
chunks.st: When the High Priest wishes to burn
chunks.stMore: the limbs of the daily offering and the accompanying meal offering, he

chunks.en: he would go up the ramp with the Segan at his right.
chunks.st: would ascend the ramp to the altar, and the deputy High Priest would walk to his right.

words.note: The Kohen who was the Kohen Gadol's helper.

chunks.en: When he reached halfway up the ramp,
chunks.st: When he reached half the height of the ramp,

chunks.en: the Segan held his right hand and brought him up.
chunks.st: the Deputy would hold his right hand and take him up to the altar at the top of the ramp.

chunks.en: The first (Kohen) handed him the head and the leg,
chunks.st: And the first of the nine priests who took the limbs up to the altar handed the High Priest the head and the hind leg of the offering,

chunks.en: and he leaned his hands on them and threw them (on the fire).
chunks.st: and the High Priest placed his hands upon them and then threw them onto the altar fire.

chunks.en: The second handed the two front legs to the first,
chunks.st: Next the second of the nine priests handed the two forelegs of the offering to the first priest.

chunks.en: who gives them to the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: He gave them to the High Priest,

chunks.en: and he leaned his hands on them and threw them.
chunks.st: who placed his hands upon them and then threw them onto the altar fire.

chunks.en: The second slipped away and left.
chunks.st: At that point, the second priest slipped away and left.

chunks.en: And this is how they would hand him
chunks.st: And in that manner the priests would hand the High Priest

chunks.en: all the rest of the parts,
chunks.st: the rest of all the limbs,

chunks.en: and he leans on them and throws them.
chunks.st: and he would place his hands upon them and then throw them onto the altar fire.

chunks.en: And when he wants,
chunks.st: And when he wishes,

chunks.en: he leans (his hands on them) and others throw them.
chunks.st: he places his hands and others throw
chunks.stMore: the limbs onto the fire. When the High Priest, who was at the top of the ramp on the south side of the altar,

chunks.en: He came to go around the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: came to circle the altar
chunks.stMore: to reach the southwestern corner, where he would pour the libation of wine,

chunks.en: From where does he begin?
chunks.st: from where does he begin?

chunks.en: From the southeast corner,
chunks.st: He begins from the southeastern corner

chunks.en: (then) the northeast,
chunks.st: and continues to the northeastern corner,

chunks.en: (then) the northwest,
chunks.st: then to the northwestern corner,

chunks.en: (then) the southwest.
chunks.st: and ultimately reaches the southwestern corner.

chunks.en: They gave him wine to pour (on the mizbe'ach).
chunks.st: At that point, the priests gave him wine to pour.

chunks.he: הַסְּגָן עוֹמֵד עַל הַקֶּרֶן וְהַסּוּדָרִים בְּיָדוֹ,
chunks.en: The Segan stands at the corner with the cloths in his hand.
chunks.st: The Deputy stands at the High Priest’s side at the corner of the altar and the cloths are in his hand,
chunks.stMore: so that he can wave them to signal to the Levites to begin singing when the High Priest pours the libation.

chunks.he: וּשְׁנֵי כֹהֲנִים עוֹמְדִים עַל שֻׁלְחַן הַחֲלָבִים
chunks.en: Two Kohanim stand at the table of the fats
chunks.st: Two priests stand at the marble table of the fats,
chunks.stMore: where the limbs and fats were placed before being taken to the altar,

chunks.en: with two silver trumpets in their hands.
chunks.st: and there were two silver trumpets in their hands.

chunks.en: They blew a tekiah, a teruah, and a tekiah.
chunks.st: These two priests sounded a tekia, a long continuous blast; they then sounded a terua, a series of staccato blasts; and lastly they sounded another tekia
chunks.stMore: to alert the Levites to prepare to recite the psalm.

chunks.en: They came and stood next to Ben Arza,
chunks.st: The priests with the trumpets came and stood near ben Arza,
chunks.stMore: the title given to the person who was tasked with striking the cymbals,

words.note: The one who played the cymbal.

chunks.en: one at his right and one at his left.
chunks.st: one to his right and one to his left.

chunks.en: He (the Kohen Gadol) bent down to pour the wine,
chunks.st: Then the High Priest stooped to pour the libation,

chunks.en: and the Segan waved the cloths,
chunks.st: and the Deputy waved the cloths,

chunks.en: and Ben Arza clanged the cymbal,
chunks.st: and ben Arza struck the cymbals,

chunks.en: and the Levi'im sang the shir.
chunks.st: and the Levites recited the psalm
chunks.stMore: of that day of the week. Each psalm was divided into three sections.

chunks.en: When they reached a break (in the song),
chunks.st: Whenever the Levites reached the end of one section of the psalm,

chunks.en: they blew (a tekiah), and the people bowed down.
chunks.st: the priests sounded a tekia, and the people in the courtyard prostrated themselves.

chunks.en: For every break,
chunks.st: At the end of each section

chunks.en: a tekiah. And for every tekiah,
chunks.st: there was a tekia, and for every tekia

chunks.en: a bowing down. This is the order of the tamid
chunks.st: there was a prostration. That is the procedure for the sacrifice of the daily offering

chunks.en: for the avodah of the House of our God.
chunks.st: in the service of the House of our God;

chunks.he: יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁיִבָּנֶה בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ, אָמֵן:
chunks.en: May it be Hashem's will that it be built quickly in our days. Amen!
chunks.st: may it be His will that it will be speedily rebuilt in our day, amen.

summary: Each day of the week the Levi'im sang a different Shir shel Yom (song of the day) in the Beis HaMikdash.
stIntro: The following is a list of each daily

chunks.en: The song that the Levi'im would say in the Beis HaMikdash:
chunks.st: psalm that the Levites would recite in the Temple.

chunks.en: On the first day (Sunday) they would say (Tehillim 24:1),
chunks.st: On the first day of the week they would recite the psalm beginning: “A psalm of David.

chunks.he: א׳), לַה' הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ תֵּבֵל וְיֹשְׁבֵי בָהּ.
chunks.en: "The earth and everything in it belongs to Hashem, the world and all who live in it."
chunks.st: The earth is the Lord’s and all it contains, the world and all who live in it” (Psalms, chapter 24).

chunks.en: On the second day they would say (Tehillim 48),
chunks.st: On the second day they would recite
chunks.stMore: the psalm beginning: “A song; a psalm of the sons of Korah.

chunks.en: "Hashem is great and very much praised
chunks.st: Great is the Lord and highly to be praised

chunks.en: in the city of our God, His holy mountain."
chunks.st: in the city of God, on His sacred mountain” (Psalms, chapter 48).

chunks.en: On the third day they would say (Tehillim 82),
chunks.st: On the third day they would recite the psalm beginning: “A psalm of Asaph.

chunks.en: "God stands among the judges;
chunks.st: God stands in the divine assembly;

chunks.en: among the judges He judges."
chunks.st: among the judges He delivers judgment” (Psalms, chapter 82).

chunks.en: On the fourth day they would say (Tehillim 94),
chunks.st: On the fourth day they would recite the psalm beginning: “

chunks.en: "A God of vengeance is Hashem, a God of
chunks.st: O Lord God, to Whom vengeance belongs, God

chunks.en: vengeance, shine forth!" and so on.
chunks.st: to Whom vengeance belongs, shine forth” (Psalms, chapter 94).

chunks.en: On the fifth day they would say (Tehillim 81),
chunks.st: On the fifth day they would recite
chunks.stMore: the psalm beginning: “For the leader; upon the Gittith, a psalm of Asaph.

chunks.en: "Sing for joy to God our strength;
chunks.st: Sing for joy to God, our strength;

chunks.en: shout to the God of Yaakov."
chunks.st: shout aloud to the God of Jacob” (Psalms, chapter 81).

chunks.en: On the sixth day they would say (Tehillim 93),
chunks.st: On the sixth day they would recite the psalm beginning: “

chunks.en: "Hashem is King, He is dressed in greatness," and so on.
chunks.st: The Lord reigns: He is robed in majesty; the Lord is robed, girded with strength” (Psalms, chapter 93).

chunks.en: On Shabbos they would say (Tehillim 92),
chunks.st: On Shabbat they would recite the psalm beginning: “

chunks.en: "A mizmor, a song for the day of Shabbos."
chunks.st: A psalm, a song for Shabbat day” (Psalms, chapter 92).

chunks.en: A song for the future to come,
chunks.st: This is interpreted as a psalm, a song for the future,

chunks.he: לְיוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת מְנוּחָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָמִים:
chunks.en: for the day that is all Shabbos and rest, for life forever.
chunks.st: for the day that will be entirely Shabbat and rest for everlasting life.
